question_text: In a current-carrying loop placed in a magnetic field, when is the torque maximum?

options.text:
(1)
When the plane of the loop is perpendicular to the field

(2)
When the plane of the loop is parallel to the field

(4)
When the magnetic field is zero

explanation:
The torque on a current-carrying loop in a magnetic field is given by τ=NIABsin⁡θ.
              It is maximum when sin⁡θ=1, i.e., θ=90∘, meaning the plane of the loop is
              perpendicular to the magnetic field.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Moving Charges and Magnetism / Test 1

question_text: Why is the magnetic field outside a long solenoid considered negligible?
explanation:
In a long solenoid, the magnetic field lines are concentrated inside, and outside, the fields from
              opposite sides of the coils cancel each other, making the external field nearly zero.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Moving Charges and Magnetism / Test 1

question_text: What is the nature of the force between two parallel wires carrying currents in opposite directions?
explanation:

              field produced by one wire interacts with the current in the other, causing them to push apart.
